headline.title: Grok 4.6 storms the frontier at half the price.
headline.summary: SpaceXAI's Grok 4.6 matches GPT-5.6 on the Intelligence Index while undercutting rivals by 60%, with Grok 4.7 teased within weeks. The model's combination of near-frontier performance and aggressive pricing is reshaping the competitive landscape.

stories.title: Grok 4.6 equals frontier models at a fraction of the cost.
stories.toc_summary: SpaceXAI's new model scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, tying GPT-5.6 and trailing only Opus 5 and Fable 5, while pricing at $2/$6 per million tokens.
stories.quick_take: SpaceXAI launched Grok 4.6, a significant upgrade over 4.5, scoring 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index—matching GPT-5.6 and trailing only Opus 5 (63) and Fable 5 (62) [1][4]. The model excels in real-world professional and legal tasks, even edging Fable, and beats Sol on coding benchmarks where 4.5 had lagged [1]. Pricing starts at $2/$6 per 1M tokens, roughly 60% cheaper than competitors, making frontier intelligence accessible at scale [1][4]. Elon Musk declared it 'objectively No. 1 when considering intelligence, speed & cost' and teased Grok 4.7 as ready in 3-4 weeks [1][2][3].

bullets.label: Benchmarks:
bullets.text: Scores 61 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, trailing Opus 5 (63) and Fable 5 (62), but ahead of Sol [1][3].

bullets.label: Cost advantage:
bullets.text: At $2/$6 per 1M tokens, it undercuts frontier rivals by 60%, with per-task cost unchanged from Grok 4.5 and comparable to open-weight Chinese models [1][2].

bullets.label: Musk's next move:
bullets.text: Grok 4.7 is slated for release in 3-4 weeks and promised to 'exceed all current models' [1][2][3].

callout.label: WHY IT MATTERS
callout.text: Grok's transition from punchline to frontier pressure is forcing rivals to respond on both performance and price. With 4.7 incoming, the competitive dynamics are set to intensify, potentially redefining what users pay for top-tier AI.

stories.title: Google Pixel 11 turns Gemini into a personal agent.
stories.toc_summary: At Made by Google 2026, the Pixel 11 with Tensor G6 enables Gemini to autonomously complete multi-step tasks across 40+ apps and adds real-time sign language translation.
stories.quick_take: Google announced the Pixel 11 lineup, powered by the new Tensor G6 chip, embedding Gemini AI more deeply [1][2]. Gemini can now handle multi-step tasks across more than 40 apps, such as booking rides, ordering groceries, and managing reservations, even on apps without native Gemini integration [2][3][4]. A standout feature is SL2T, a DeepMind model that translates American Sign Language into text in real time, developed with the deaf community [3][4]. Google also unveiled a $29 Pixel Tag to rival AirTag and introduced Live Translate for real-time video and audio translation [1][2].

bullets.label: On-device AI:
bullets.text: Tensor G6 enables many Gemini features to run locally, reducing latency and improving privacy [3][4].

bullets.label: Agentic actions:
bullets.text: Gemini can autonomously complete tasks like making calls or booking services, marking a shift from reactive assistant to proactive agent [3][4].

bullets.label: Accessibility milestone:
bullets.text: SL2T translates American Sign Language into English on-device, turning visual gestures into native input [3][4].

callout.label: BIG PICTURE
callout.text: The Pixel 11 represents Google's bet that AI agents will move from the cloud into daily hardware, making hands-free, autonomous assistance mainstream and reshaping consumer expectations.

stories.title: Claude in Chrome brings browser agents to your workflow.
stories.toc_summary: Anthropic's Claude now works as a Chrome side panel, letting users start tasks in Claude Cowork and continue them in the browser, where the agent can click, type, and scan pages.
stories.quick_take: Anthropic rolled out 'Claude in Chrome,' a side panel that extends Claude Cowork's desktop agent capabilities into the browser [1]. This allows users to launch tasks in Claude and resume them in a web interface where the AI can interact with pages [1]. The update is available on paid plans, with sessions tied to the account so progress follows the user across devices [2]. However, Anthropic warns of prompt injection risks, where embedded instructions could hijack the agent, urging users to manually confirm critical steps [2][3].

bullets.label: Cross-device continuity:
bullets.text: Sessions persist via the account, enabling seamless task continuation between desktop, mobile, and web [2].

bullets.label: Web interaction:
bullets.text: The agent can click, type, and scan pages, effectively turning the browser into a hands-on AI workspace [1].

bullets.label: Security caution:
bullets.text: Anthropic highlights the risk of embedded instructions hijacking browser agents, advising manual confirmation for critical actions [2][3].

callout.label: WHAT TO WATCH
callout.text: As browser agents become more capable, they also become a prime target for prompt injection attacks. Enterprises must adopt robust guardrails to safely integrate these tools.

stories.title: DeepSeek releases open-source agent framework with MIT license.
stories.toc_summary: DeepSeek's Harness v0.1, an agent-building framework, is now freely available on GitHub under MIT license, enabling commercial use and fostering an open alternative to proprietary agent infrastructure.
stories.quick_take: DeepSeek open-sourced its agent framework, Harness v0.1, under the MIT license, allowing unrestricted commercial use [1]. The framework, built on the Cordis-Meta system, provides the tools to construct and deploy autonomous AI agents [1]. This move contrasts with OpenAI and Google, which keep agent infrastructure behind APIs and paywalls, potentially democratizing agent development [1][2]. The release could accelerate innovation in agent-based applications across industries [1].

bullets.label: Full access:
bullets.text: Complete code is on GitHub with MIT license, including commercial use rights [1].

bullets.label: Strategic contrast:
bullets.text: While US labs monetize agent infrastructure, DeepSeek gives it away, undercutting the proprietary ecosystem [1][2].

bullets.label: Potential impact:
bullets.text: Lowering barriers could spur a wave of new agent applications and research, particularly in markets where cost is a barrier [1][2].

callout.label: LONG ARC
callout.text: DeepSeek's open-source move signals a broader trend toward democratizing AI infrastructure, challenging the closed approaches of Western labs and potentially reshaping the global AI supply chain.

stories.title: Nvidia market cap surges past Apple by a trillion.
stories.toc_summary: Nvidia's market value now exceeds Apple's by $1 trillion, driven by soaring AI compute demand and record-high Blackwell chip prices auctioned by Nebius.
stories.quick_take: In under two weeks, Nvidia's market cap has leapfrogged Apple by $1 trillion, with Nvidia gaining 18% while Apple fell ~10% [1]. The surge is fueled by the booming market for AI compute, where Nebius's Q2 auction saw Blackwell chip prices 15% above any prior asking [1]. Deliberate scarcity management—selling capacity only shortly before demand—has intensified the premium [1]. This highlights AI infrastructure as a supercycle rather than a fleeting trend, with Nvidia's dominance now extending into cloud economics [1].

bullets.label: Market cap shift:
bullets.text: Nvidia is now $1T more valuable than Apple, reversing its position from two weeks ago [1].

bullets.label: Compute demand:
bullets.text: Nebius's auction set record Blackwell prices, indicating severe supply-demand imbalance [1].

bullets.label: Strategic scarcity:
bullets.text: Sellers are deliberately limiting capacity, driving prices and reinforcing Nvidia's pricing power [1].

callout.label: WHY IT MATTERS
callout.text: Nvidia's valuation is now tied to AI's long-term infrastructure needs, making it a barometer for the entire sector. The sustained premium suggests investors believe the compute demand is structural, not speculative.

stories.title: AI-crafted cancer vaccine for a dog spawns a startup.
stories.toc_summary: After using ChatGPT and AlphaFold to create a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine for his dog Rosie, Paul Conyngham founded YC-backed Gamgee to offer similar treatments worldwide.
stories.quick_take: Paul Conyngham's journey from building a cancer vaccine for his dog Rosie with AI tools to founding Gamgee highlights AI's power to accelerate personalized medicine [1]. Rosie's aggressive mast cell cancer defied conventional treatments, but an AI-designed vaccine developed with UNSW reduced tumors [1]. Sam Altman's encouragement led to Gamgee, now backed by Y Combinator [1]. The company is conducting first trials in Australia and accepting cases globally, managing the entire process from design to monitoring [1].

bullets.label: Personalized approach:
bullets.text: The vaccine targets the specific mutations in each dog's tumor, using AI to analyze genomic data [1].

bullets.label: AI-driven discovery:
bullets.text: Conyngham leveraged ChatGPT and AlphaFold for scientific and analytical tasks, demonstrating accessible AI-driven biotech [1].

bullets.label: From pet to human:
bullets.text: The hope is that this startup will pave the way for similar personalized cancer treatments in humans [1].

callout.label: DO THIS TODAY
callout.text: The story underscores the 'just do it' ethos of the AI age—individuals can now leverage AI to tackle complex problems previously accessible only to large institutions. Consider how AI could accelerate projects in your own field.

editorial.title: The era of accessible superintelligence begins now.
editorial.intro: Today's stories paint a clear picture: AI is becoming both cheaper and more capable at an unprecedented pace.
editorial.body: Grok 4.6's near-frontier performance at half the price signals a shift from exclusive intelligence to mass-market commodity [1][2]. Meanwhile, open-source frameworks from DeepSeek and on-device agents from Google are breaking down barriers to adoption. The race isn't just about who builds the smartest model—it's about who can democratize access, making superintelligence a tool for everyone. Nvidia's market cap surge underscores that the infrastructure fueling this is just getting started.
editorial.pull_quote: Frontier intelligence is becoming a commodity—whoever distributes it cheapest wins the next era.
editorial.outro: As these forces converge, the pace of change will only accelerate. The winners will be those who adapt quickly and leverage AI's new accessibility to transform their own work and life.

takeaway.label: IF YOU TAKE ONE THING FROM THIS
takeaway.text: The cost of top-tier AI is plummeting while capabilities keep climbing. Today is the day to experiment with new tools like Grok 4.6 or browser agents—because in six months, they may be table stakes.
